title: Story Skills Schema v2
$comment: Entity ids are filename-derived: the kebab-case basename of the entity file without .md (e.g. characters/sera-voss.md -> sera-voss). Frontmatter never carries a separate id field; the required id in each definition below is that filename-derived identifier as it appears in reference lists and registries.

allOf.$comment: Without a story.md calendar, a chapter or scene date shaped YYYY-MM-DD must be a real day. With one (calendar is set), story validate reads such a date as a day of that calendar instead, so the schema leaves it free.

story.$comment: writing-mode vertical and chapter-numerals native need a language that has them; without language the book is English, which has neither. For each, the language pattern is generated by scripts/schema-patterns.js from the language, script, and numeral tables story validate reads (supportsVertical, nativeNumerals), so it accepts exactly the tags validate does. For writing-mode vertical: one with a script subtag set vertically (zh-Hant, ja-Jpan), or else a language written vertically (ja, ko, zh, yue, zh-yue). For chapter-numerals native: one whose script has its own numerals (ar, fa, hi, th, ja, zh, az-IR, mn-Mong), but not Korean (ko-Hani).

target-characters.description: Target length in characters, measured when the book counts characters (count-unit).

count-unit.description: The unit lengths are counted in. Defaults from the language: characters for Chinese (zh) and Japanese (ja), words otherwise.

language.description: A BCP 47 tag such as en, en-GB, or fr-CA; a [TODO] placeholder means not set yet (English), which story validate warns about.

publication-date.$comment: The day is the pattern of #/$defs/realDate, generated by scripts/schema-patterns.js.
publication-date.description: A real calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD; blank or a [TODO] placeholder means not set yet, which story validate warns about.

subjects.description: BISAC subject codes such as FIC022000; a [TODO] placeholder is not set yet, which story validate warns about.

ifid.description: Interactive fiction id (a version 4 UUID) for build --format twee; without it the build derives a stable one from the story id.

chapter-label.description: Word for generated chapter headings, such as Kapitel; {n} places the number. Defaults to the language pack's word (Chapter in English). Same as a labels chapter entry, which wins.

writing-mode.description: How builds set the text. vertical sets columns top to bottom, right to left, with pages turned right to left; story validate allows it only for a language written that way, such as ja, zh, zh-Hant, or ko. Defaults to horizontal.

chapter-numerals.description: Numerals for the numbers in generated chapter headings. native prints the language's own: Han numerals in Japanese and Chinese (第十二章), the script's digits in Arabic, Persian, Hindi, Thai, and others; story validate allows it only for a language that has them. Ids, file names, and anchors keep 0-9. Defaults to western.

contents-label.description: Heading for generated tables of contents, such as Inhalt. Defaults to the language pack's heading (Contents in English). Same as a labels contents entry, which wins.

labels.description: Overrides for the generated text in builds, as - key: text entries; {name} places a value. The language pack (from language) supplies the defaults, English where it has none. labels wins over chapter-label and contents-label. story validate warns about a key that is not listed here.

editor.description: The editor of a collection or anthology: a name or a list of names. Title pages credit them with the edited-by label, and the EPUB names them as creators with the edt role.

cover.description: Cover image path relative to story.md: a .gif, .jpeg, .jpg, .png, or .webp file. story validate also checks the file exists.

daily-target-words.description: Words a writing day aims for; story progress measures today and the streak against it.

daily-target-characters.description: Characters a writing day aims for, measured when the book counts characters (count-unit).

writing-days.description: The weekdays you plan to write (mon to sun, or full names). Other days never break the story progress streak. Unset or an empty list means every day.

release-every.description: Serial release cadence: days between episodes, such as 7 for weekly, or months from 1 to 999999, such as 1 month: the same day each month, or the month's last day when it is shorter. Needs release-start. story progress and story next show the next episode due and warn when one close or past has no prose.

release-start.description: The real-world YYYY-MM-DD day episode 1 (the first chapter) releases, even in a book with a story calendar. Needs release-every.

release-warn-days.description: Serial: how many days before its release date story progress and story next warn about an episode with no prose (release-undrafted). Default 3; 0 warns only from the day it is due.

calendar.description: A secondary world's calendar, as a list of entries in order: each month (- month: Thaw then days: 30), an optional weekdays entry (- weekdays: [Hearthday, Stoneday] with an optional first-weekday, the weekday of the first day of year 1), and optional eras (- era: Age of Embers with abbrev, direction forward or backward, and years). Chapter and scene dates are then written under it, such as 3 Thaw 301 AE or 301-02-03 AE. story validate also rejects an entry that names none or more than one of month, era, and weekdays, repeated names, no months, a backward era that is not the first, and a forward era other than the last without years.

build-style.description: How the EPUB, HTML review copy, and print interior look: a list of mappings, usually one, whose keys together give a preset and any overrides. Unset, builds keep their classic look. The Shunn manuscript and DOCX builds never read it. story validate rejects an unknown key, a key set twice, and a css file that is missing or outside the project.

preset.description: classic (the default look), modern, or elegant.

body-font.description: The body text font for the EPUB, HTML review copy, and print interior: comma-separated font names, such as Iowan Old Style, Georgia, serif.

heading-font.description: The chapter heading font for the EPUB, HTML review copy, and print interior: comma-separated font names, such as Iowan Old Style, Georgia, serif.

heading-style.description: Chapter headings centred, centred in small capitals, or bold and flush with the start of the line.

scene-break.description: The text a scene break prints, such as * * * or a fleuron: one line.

drop-caps.description: A drop cap at the start of each chapter, in a script with capitals.

paragraphs.description: Paragraphs with a first-line indent, or as blocks with space between them.

css.description: An extra stylesheet relative to story.md, inside the project, added after the build's own rules. story validate also checks the file exists.

cli-defaults.description: Default flags per story command. Each entry names a command that takes a project; its other keys are flags that command accepts, without the leading --. A flag given on the command line always wins. story validate rejects unknown commands and flags.

severity.description: Promote a named warning to an error, or turn it off (it is then reported as dismissed).

queries.description: Saved filters that story list --query <name> runs. Each entry gives a kebab-case name, unique in the list; the kind it lists, plural or singular as story list takes it; and where, a flow list of one or more --where filters (key=value, key!=value, key, or "!key"), all of which must match, such as where: [status=draft, pov=mara-quill]. story validate also rejects any other key, an empty where, and a filter on a key the kind neither defines nor any of its files sets.

id.description: Filename-derived identifier: the kebab-case basename of the entity file without .md. There is no separate id frontmatter field.

calendarName.description: A calendar month, weekday, era, or era abbreviation: it starts with something other than a digit and holds no comma.

names.description: A name, or a list of names.

realDate.$comment: Generated by scripts/schema-patterns.js from parseClockDate, which story validate runs: a YYYY-MM-DD day that exists, with 29 February only in a leap year (a year divisible by 4, except a century year not divisible by 400, so 2000 but not 1900). Spaces around it are allowed, as validate trims them.
realDate.description: A real calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2024-02-29.

realDateOrText.$comment: Generated by scripts/schema-patterns.js: any text, except that text shaped YYYY-MM-DD (spaces around it allowed) must be a real day, as for realDate. It sits beside the chapter and scene date's own type, so it checks only the pattern.

numbered.description: false builds the chapter under its title alone (a Prologue or Epilogue) and leaves it out of the printed chapter count.

author.description: The author of this chapter, for a story in a collection or anthology: a name or a list of names. Builds print it under the heading with the byline label, it never counts toward word counts, and the EPUB lists it as a contributor.

character-count.description: Characters of prose, which story wordcount --write records when the book counts characters.

mode.description: How the chapter was written. story add chapter writes an empty mode, which means unset.

date.description: Story date as YYYY-MM-DD. Without a story.md calendar, a value in that shape must be a real calendar day (not 2024-13-45 or 2023-02-29); with one, story validate reads it as a day of that calendar. story continuity warns about other text.

beat.description: The beat-sheet beat the chapter carries, as free text: a name from the plot-structure skill's beat sheets (Inciting Incident, Midpoint, All Is Lost) or the writer's own. story grid, story context, and the codex show it; story validate warns above 60 characters (grapheme clusters).

release-date.description: Serial: the real-world YYYY-MM-DD day this episode releases, even in a book with a story calendar. Overrides the story.md release-every cadence for this chapter only.

choices.description: Branching: the choices that end this chapter, each leading to another chapter. Once any chapter has choices, a chapter without them is an ending. build --format twee turns them into Twine links.

text.description: The words the reader picks; no [, ], |, ->, <-, or line break, and no final <, which Twine reads as link syntax.

date.description: Story date as YYYY-MM-DD. Without a story.md calendar, a value in that shape must be a real calendar day (not 2024-13-45 or 2023-02-29); with one, story validate reads it as a day of that calendar. story continuity warns about other text.

progressions.description: Timeline-scoped changes to a character, location, or faction. The frontmatter describes the entity as the story opens; from the chapter in from onward (in story time), field holds value instead. Entries are listed in story order, and field names a single-value field, never a list field, id, progressions, died-in, or revived-in.

progressLog.description: Optional progress.md frontmatter: one manuscript word count per logged day, written by story progress --log.

characters.description: The manuscript in characters, logged when the book counts characters.

research.description: Research note in research/: a fact the story relies on, its sources, and the chapters that use it.

matter.description: Front or back matter in matter/: dedication, epigraph, acknowledgments, author's note, about the author.

styleWordLists.$comment: Each value is words separated by commas, a flow list such as [sintió, vio], or [] for none. story validate warns about a list name it does not know (unknown-word-list).

styleSheet.description: Optional style-sheet.md frontmatter: house spelling and usage decisions enforced by story prose.

replace-words.description: Replaces language-pack word lists, as - list-name: word, word entries ([] empties a list), such as - filter-words: sintió, vio.

add-words.description: Adds words to language-pack word lists, as - list-name: word, word entries, such as - said-bookisms: rugió.

samples.description: Files or folders of the author's own prose, relative to the project folder (such as ../book-one), that story prose builds a baseline from.

exemption.$comment: An entry matches a finding when every key it sets matches. story validate also requires a pattern, or a code with a file, chapter, or pattern; refuses a chapter with a code whose findings carry none, and a misspelled key; entries it rejects never take effect.

pattern.description: Text the finding's message contains, as a case-sensitive substring; / and \ in paths match either separator.

code.description: The finding's code: any warning a story.md severity entry can name, or an error story continuity reports.

file.description: The project file the finding is about, relative to story.md, such as chapters/chapter-03.md: no absolute path and no .. segment.

chapter.description: The chapter a finding that carries a chapter shows up in, such as chapter-03.
